data.title: bn-3gx: M1.6.1 `lead add` and the lead dispositions, including import from Teapot

data.body: [HIGH] Do not infer semantic principal roles from the captured flow's session or fill every remaining principal slot from map order. Teapot exposes the session that carried the flow, but that does not establish that principal as the object's ; with three or more declared principals,  also selects an arbitrary  and reuses it for every non-owner principal slot. I reproduced this at the exact target by changing only flow 12's session from  to : the generated complete plan silently changed  from alice to bob. This can drive later verification under the wrong principals.  may fill only facts the flow actually supplies (route/property/session identity); require explicit operator/lead role binding or a declared unambiguous mapping before claiming a complete plan.

[HIGH] Page through every matching session result (or use an exact metadata query) before returning . The pinned Teapot  documents  as at most 1000 and exposes  specifically to continue from the prior  cursor. This code makes exactly one  call per session and ignores pagination, so a valid flow after the first 1000 matching rows is silently reported missing. That breaks  for ordinary long-lived sessions and makes the result depend on capture volume rather than the requested ID.

[MEDIUM] Reject an invalid user-supplied disposition/update reason instead of silently replacing it with . I reproduced this at the exact target by passing : the command succeeded and appended an event whose reason was the fallback, losing the operator's supplied attribution text. Append-only attributed history must either preserve a valid reason exactly or return a usage error without committing; silently manufacturing audit text makes the event record misleading. The same helper affects set, withdraw, defer, and duplicate.

Correction (shell-safe complete text): [HIGH] Do not infer semantic principal roles from the captured flow session or fill every remaining principal slot from map order. Teapot exposes the session that carried the flow, but that does not establish that principal as the object owner; with three or more declared principals, the first non-owner map entry is also selected arbitrarily and reused for every non-owner principal slot. At the exact target, changing only flow 12 from session.alice to session.bob silently changed the generated complete plan owner from alice to bob. This can drive later verification under the wrong principals. Flow intake may fill only facts the flow actually supplies (route, property, session identity); require explicit role binding or a declared unambiguous mapping before claiming a complete plan.

Correction (shell-safe complete text): [HIGH] Page through every matching session result, or use an exact metadata query, before returning OBJECT_NOT_FOUND. Pinned Teapot FlowsListArgs documents a maximum limit of 1000 and an after cursor for the next page. This code makes exactly one oldest-first call per session and ignores pagination, so a valid flow after the first 1000 matching rows is silently reported missing. That breaks lead add with a flow ID for ordinary long-lived sessions and makes the result depend on capture volume rather than the requested ID.

Correction (shell-safe complete text): [MEDIUM] Reject an invalid user-supplied disposition or update reason instead of silently replacing it with the words lead event. At the exact target, a defer reason containing a newline succeeded and appended the fallback reason, losing the operator supplied attribution text. Append-only attributed history must preserve a valid reason exactly or return a usage error without committing; manufacturing audit text makes the record misleading. The same helper affects set, withdraw, defer, and duplicate.

data.reason: Exact target is not acceptance-ready: flow intake invents owner and other role bindings, passive flow lookup drops valid IDs beyond Teapot's first 1000-row page, and invalid disposition reasons commit silently rewritten audit text. See the three open threads.

data.body: Fixed in 894a096: flow intake now treats the captured session only as a declared identity hint and never assigns it to owner/other. A flow-derived class requires every principal role as an explicit validated --slot; absent roles return SLOTS_INCOMPLETE and ambiguous/duplicate principals remain refused before target traffic. The no-traffic socket witness now covers the refusal and the explicit complete-plan path.

Fixed in 894a096: passive flow lookup follows Teapot next-page advice with --after, validates numeric cursors, rejects duplicate/multiple malformed cursors, and enforces an aggregate 1024-page bound as a typed DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE failure rather than OBJECT_NOT_FOUND. Regression flow 1012 is found only after a full 1000-row first page.

Fixed in 894a096: the shared event constructor rejects empty or control-bearing reasons with USAGE_ERROR instead of substituting text. Process/store regression covers set, withdraw, defer, and duplicate and proves revision, lead text, and append-only event history remain unchanged.

Verified at 894a096f2a294030de37b361b2f6f2335eb34a46. The exact test refuses omitted roles with SLOTS_INCOMPLETE and no target socket connection, while explicit distinct roles produce a complete passive plan. In a disposable exact-target regression I moved flow 1012 from Alice's session to Bob's session; the stored owner remained explicit Alice and other remained explicit Bob, proving captured session identity no longer assigns semantic roles. Resolved.

Verified at 894a096f2a294030de37b361b2f6f2335eb34a46. The exact test finds flow 1012 only after the full 1000-row first page and records the after 1000 invocation. A disposable exact-target regression proved a repeated cursor returns INTEGRITY_FAILURE after two pages, and a monotonic cursor stream returns DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE after exactly 1024 additional page calls; neither path connected to the target socket. Resolved.

Verified at 894a096f2a294030de37b361b2f6f2335eb34a46. Exact process coverage passes a control-bearing reason through set, withdraw, defer, and duplicate; each returns USAGE_ERROR and leaves lead revision, text, and append-only event history byte-for-byte unchanged. Resolved.
